Hi Olivia — thanks for sending the redlines. Quick summary of the internal position so we can get aligned before we escalate to legal: 

- Operator/admin keys: Redwood policy is to not retain unlimited operator keys post‑handover for on‑prem deployments. Typical options we offer: a) full handoff of keys (customer custody) + signed attestation of build provenance; or b) Redwood retains a limited emergency operator access token with approval process and constrained timebound sessions (audit logged).
- Escrow/attestation: We can provide a build provenance package (hashes, reproducible build instructions) and an independent attestation report from our packaging/ops team. Full code escrow is not standard for our commercial on‑prem offering and would need legal/engineering discussion and cost allocation.
- Remote evidence: we can agree to a scheduled evidence snapshot (weekly or on‑demand with a signed request) delivered over SFTP to your secure bucket, plus on‑site review windows. Continuous remote management or persistent reverse‑SSH is not something we accept for air‑gapped installs.

I'll loop in Monica (Customer Success) and Karthik (Legal liaison) to coordinate a concise redline response. Can we set a mini‑sync Thu 5/27 10am PT to walk legal through our proposed text?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Manager, Solutions — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Phone: (415) 555‑0192

Subject: Re: On‑prem deployment — operator access & evidence request

Hi all — I joined the call and wanted to capture the action items and a pragmatic path forward I proposed on the call: 

1) Operator keys: propose contract language that requires (a) full key handover to Acme with documented operators, OR (b) emergency‑only remote access limited to 2 sessions/year, each session <= 2 hours, pre‑approved by Acme security and logged.
2) Evidence package: deliverable list — (i) signed SBOM + build hashes, (ii) reproducible build instructions, (iii) signed binary attestation from Redwood ops. This package will be delivered via SFTP or in person.
3) Escrow alternative: Redwood to propose a neutral third‑party attestation vendor (we can share 2 vendors we have worked with) rather than code escrow; vendor costs to be borne by Acme or shared (TBD).
4) Audit windows: propose weekly automated snapshot + ad‑hoc snapshot on request (48hr SLA to schedule). Remote execution requires joint admin session; no unattended persistent tunnels.

Next steps: Karthik to produce draft redline snippets for the MSA and Order Form capturing #1–#4. Aditya — can you please pull a sample ops attestation package and vendor contact list by Monday 5/31? Olivia — if procurement needs an estimated commercial uplift for escrow/attestation vendor we can put a placeholder line item.

—Monica
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Olivia / Acme team — attaching a concise set of legal‑grade redline snippets we recommend to be inserted into the MSA (Section 7: Deployment & Control) and the Order Form. Highlights: 

- "Operator Access": define as emergency‑only with explicit session caps OR customer custody; include pre‑approval and two‑person auth for sessions.
- Escrow/Attestation: insert alternative language that Redwood will provide a third‑party attestation report (scope defined) in lieu of source code escrow. If Acme insists on escrow, we need to table and assess IP/seq obligations and pricing.
- Audit/Evidence Delivery: agree to scheduled snapshots delivered to Acme's SFTP with integrity hashes; any on‑site inspection is subject to mutually agreed scope and confidentiality controls.

I have attached the draft snippets (as text in the attachment). Please review and let us know which of the emergency access vs. full custody options Acme prefers — that choice materially changes commercial terms.

Regards,
